hypotheses.reasoning: The 500s on POST /v1/notify come from notification-svc, which fails because template-svc cannot render: its artifact write to S3 (s3://notifications-artifacts-prod, us-east-1) fails. The first anomaly is #3430 at 17:43:26Z: template-svc gets a 503 ServiceUnavailable from S3 on the upload of m-5550.json. Before that, template-svc /render calls were succeeding (e.g. #3428 ok 35ms, #3429 notify 200). The S3 errors then continue as 503 (#3536) and 500 InternalError (#3792, #3925), so the failures are fast explicit errors from S3, not hangs. notification-svc then reports 'TemplateClient.render failed: template-svc returned 500 (storage write failed)' (#3527, #3785, #4295), and api-gateway returns 500 with 5-28s latency (#3709, #4044). The aws-sdk retry quota exhaustion (#3656: 59 failed attempts in 60s) shows retries amplifying load, but the trigger is S3 itself. No config or deploy change appears near onset. Ruled out or secondary: flag-sync 'unknown flag in staging-2' errors (#991 etc.) are noise that keeps the cached value; metrics-agent queue drops are a symptom of the wider backlog; status-poller has no errors. Caveat: the status page did not show an S3 incident, so this rests on log evidence alone.

A separate fault: event-processor repeatedly fails on msg-856174 at partition 5, offset 141656, because the JSON payload contains a NUL byte at position 292 (#3759, #4071, #4294). This is a real problem and causes ingest-api events to time out waiting for downstream confirmation (#4298). It starts after the S3 failures begin, however, and it does not produce the notify 500s, which come from template-svc/notification-svc, so it is not the root cause of the alert.

verdict.recommendedAction: Confirm the AWS S3 us-east-1 incident (request IDs B0782E6, B7D69DB, 7F70173). Mitigate by failing over or degrading template artifact writes (for example, render inline without the S3 artifact, or queue artifact uploads for retry) and by reducing SDK retry amplification. Once S3 recovers, drain the backlog. Separately, fix the poison message msg-856174 (NUL byte at offset 141656, partition 5) in event-processor (#3759, #4071, #4294). It is a parallel issue that explains the ingest-api 120s confirmation timeouts (#4298, #4425).

hypotheses.reasoning: The 500s on POST /v1/notify come from notification-svc, which fails because template-svc cannot render: its artifact write to S3 (s3://notifications-artifacts-prod, us-east-1) fails. The first anomaly is #3430 at 17:43:26Z: template-svc gets a 503 ServiceUnavailable from S3 on the upload of m-5550.json. Before that, template-svc /render calls were succeeding (e.g. #3428 ok 35ms, #3429 notify 200). The S3 errors then continue as 503 (#3536) and 500 InternalError (#3792, #3925), so the failures are fast explicit errors from S3, not hangs. notification-svc then reports 'TemplateClient.render failed: template-svc returned 500 (storage write failed)' (#3527, #3785, #4295), and api-gateway returns 500 with 5–28s latency (#3709, #4044). The aws-sdk retry quota exhaustion (#3656: 59 failed attempts in 60s) shows the retries amplifying the load, but the trigger is S3 itself. No config or deploy change appears near onset. Ruled out or secondary: flag-sync 'unknown flag in staging-2' errors (#991 etc.) are noise that keeps the cached value; metrics-agent queue drops are a symptom of the wider backlog; status-poller has no errors. Caveat: the status page did not show an S3 incident, so this rests on the log evidence alone.
hypotheses.recommendedAction: Confirm the AWS S3 us-east-1 incident (request IDs B0782E6, B7D69DB, 7F70173). Mitigate by failing over or degrading template artifact writes (for example, serve the render inline without the S3 artifact, or queue artifact uploads for retry) and by reducing SDK retry amplification. Once S3 recovers, drain the backlog. Separately, fix the poison message msg-856174 (NUL byte at offset 141656, partition 5) in event-processor (#3759, #4071, #4294). It is a parallel issue that explains the ingest-api 120s confirmation timeouts (#4298, #4425).

hypotheses.reasoning: A separate fault: event-processor repeatedly fails on msg-856174 at partition 5, offset 141656, because the JSON payload contains a NUL byte at position 292 (#3759, #4071, #4294). This is a real problem and causes ingest-api events to time out waiting for downstream confirmation (#4298). It starts after the S3 failures begin, however, and it does not produce the notify 500s, which come from template-svc/notification-svc, so it is not the root cause of the alert.
